doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Tony Bennett in the studio
summary: Bucky recorded with Bennett often, and Bennett missed the John Bunch session by minutes but liked the recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let me toss a couple of names at you here, and get some personal comments. Tony Bennett?

Oh Tony. I made a lot of recordings with Tony. With about five or six different leaders. And I still see Tony on the street once in a while and we talk. In fact when we did the Tony Bennett songs with John Bunch, we called him to come to the studio see? And he wasn’t home so John left a message. We’re over at the Nola Studios, you know, Steinway Hall, on 57th Street. And we finished the session and went home. Two minutes later Tony Bennett walks up to the studio. Where are the guys? They went home.
So they gave him a copy of the record to listen to. So he and John got together, I don’t know. He sort of liked it.
Good. Is he a pro in the studio?
Oh yeah, yeah. He knows exactly what he wants.
